note: ShelfCheck compilation double-count structural audit. Local-data-only audit (plus a small number of targeted PS Store lookups for the Tomb Raider cover fix specifically, not for census structure). Checked two detection patterns: (1) every multi-identity product whose own title ALSO exists as a separate census identity -- 48 multi-identity products total, 43 with a same-titled identity, all 43 correctly EXCLUDED (not double-counted); (2) every INCLUDED identity whose title is another INCLUDED identity's title plus a remaster/edition-style suffix -- 2 candidate pairs found, both verified (via genuine franchise knowledge, not guesswork) to be different games that happen to share a title fragment, not duplicates. A third case (River City Melee / Battle Royal Special) was found via the Phase 3 explicit-checklist, not either automated pattern -- it has no DATA.p product link at all, so neither detector could see it; it was identified via the cover-sourcing research from the prior pass. NO census changes were made in this audit. NO merges/exclusions were applied.

tombRaiderPhase1.finding: NO double-count found. Tomb Raider I-III/IV-VI Remastered already exist as census identities (#1805, #1806) but are correctly EXCLUDED -- they do not count toward the denominator. They ALSO exist as DATA.p products that correctly satisfy the 6 individual classic-game component identities. This is the intended model working correctly; the 2013+ reboot trilogy (Definitive Edition / Rise / Shadow) is a separate, genuinely distinct set of games, not a duplicate of the classic trilogy.
tombRaiderPhase1.coverIssueFound: Identity #2196 (Tomb Raider III) had no cover at all. Identities #2194, #2195, #2197, #2198, #2199 had covers from automated IGDB exact-title matching, but per-game (not necessarily reflecting the actual owned physical PS4 product, the remastered collection). Fixed in this pass: all 6 component identities now use their respective remastered-collection's official PS Store cover, consistently, per explicit instruction to have them "inherit/reuse that product cover consistently."

remasterSuffixAudit.reasoning: "Call of Duty: Modern Warfare" (#221, 2019 Infinity Ward reboot) and "Call of Duty: Modern Warfare Remastered" (#222, 2016 remaster of the ORIGINAL 2007 "Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare") are two entirely different games with different campaigns/multiplayer that happen to share a near-identical title due to franchise branding. Not a duplicate.

"Final Fantasy VII" (#479, the 1997 original) is EXCLUDED, and "Final Fantasy VII Remake" (#480) is a ground-up reimagining released as its own multi-part game, not a remaster of the same content. No denominator risk since the base identity is not INCLUDED at all.

"Tomb Raider" (#2194, the 1996 classic, part of the "Tomb Raider I-III Remastered" trilogy) and "Tomb Raider: Definitive Edition" (#1339, the PS4 port of the 2013 Crystal Dynamics reboot, first entry in the Rise/Shadow of the Tomb Raider trilogy) are two entirely different games from different eras of the franchise that happen to share the base word "Tomb Raider". Not a duplicate.

identityB.title: River City Melee: Battle Royal Special

safeDuplicates.reasoning: Verified via Limited Run Games' own store listing ("Limited Run #103: River City Melee (PS4)") and eStarland's listing of the same LRG #103 catalog number explicitly as "River City Melee: Battle Royal Special" -- these are two title renderings of the SAME single physical PS4 disc, not two different games or editions. No DATA.p product entry currently links them (unlike every other compilation in this census), so they are tracked as two fully independent completion identities today.
safeDuplicates.currentOwnershipEffect: Josh's GameEye collection lists exactly one title, "River City Melee", which exact-matches only identity #1003. #1710 shows as unsatisfied/missing even though the one physical disc Josh owns is the same game.
